sn5.9:1.2: Then, in the morning, the bhikkhuni Sela dressed …
sn5.9:1.3: she sat down at the foot of a tree for the day’s abiding.
sn5.9:1.4: Then Mara the Evil One, desiring to arouse fear, trepidation, and terror in the bhikkhuni Sela, desiring to make her fall away from concentration,
sn5.9:1.5: approached her and addressed her in verse:
sn5.9:2.1: By whom has this puppet been created?
sn5.9:2.2: Where is the maker of the puppet?
sn5.9:3.1: Then it occurred to the bhikkhuni Sela:
sn5.9:3.4: This is Mara the Evil One … desiring to make me fall away from concentration.”
sn5.9:3.5: Then the bhikkhuni Sela, having understood, “This is Mara the Evil One,” replied to him in verses:
sn5.9:4.1: “This puppet is not made by itself,
sn5.9:4.2: Nor is this misery made by another.
sn5.9:4.3: It has come to be dependent on a cause;
sn5.9:4.4: With the cause’s breakup it will cease.

It grows depending on a pair of factors:
sn5.9:5.3: It requires both the soil’s nutrients
sn5.9:5.4: And a steady supply of moisture:
sn5.9:6.2: And these six bases of sensory contact,
sn5.9:6.3: Have come to be dependent on a cause;
sn5.9:6.4: With the cause’s breakup they will cease.”
sn5.9:7.1: Then Mara the Evil One, realizing, “The bhikkhuni Sela knows me,” sad and disappointed, disappeared right there.
